clue.text: Get up in cold wing

blocks.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a wing is a bird's limb

explanation.surface: Someone told to rise and dress for a chilly part of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb is to ascend, which is a synonym of getting up.

clue.text: Ring everybody after end of epic

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only that one is kept
coming after something places it second, which fixes the order of the parts

blocks.note: the final letter of epic
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Phoning everyone once a long story has finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone is to telephone them, a synonym of calling.

clue.text: Paid no attention to grid, one printed incorrectly

indicators.note: a misprint puts letters in the wrong places, so these are to be rearranged

blocks.note: the two words supply the letters

explanation.surface: A solver who disregarded a crossword grid because one was misprinted.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to pay it no heed, so the past tense matches paid no attention to.

clue.text: Cocktail made up by British boys

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
two boys' names, Randy and Alexander

explanation.surface: A drink mixed by some young British lads.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brandy Alexander is a creamy mixed drink of brandy, crème de cacao and cream, so it is an example of a cocktail.

clue.text: Drake, thus, spliced knot

indicators.note: rope that is spliced has its strands unwoven and interlaced again, so the letters are rewoven in a new order

blocks.note: the two words supply the letters

explanation.surface: Sir Francis Drake, the sailor, splicing rope into a knot.
explanation.walkthrough: Drake suggests the Elizabethan seafarer, which makes knots and splicing look natural, but his name is only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A Turk's head is a decorative sailor's knot shaped like a turban, so it is an example of a knot.

clue.text: Poke fun at head of eating-house following meals

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept
following something means coming after it, which sets the order of the two parts

blocks.note: tea is an afternoon or evening meal in Britain
the opening letter of eating-house

explanation.surface: Mocking the owner of a café after dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To tease someone is to make fun of them playfully.

clue.text: Amend drawing to include new flag

indicators.note: to include something is to take it within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to amend a drawing is to redesign it
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Revising a sketch so that it shows a newly designed banner.
explanation.walkthrough: The extra letter goes in after the fourth letter, splitting the word into a colour and a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Ensign is the flag flown by British merchant ships, so it is an example of a flag.

clue.text: Girl got mounts over a jumps racetrack here in New York

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means climbing upward, so the word is read from bottom to top
in a down clue, one part over another sits above it, fixing the order

blocks.note: Sara is a girl's name
taken as written before being turned upward
taken as written
springs means leaps or jumps

explanation.surface: A girl's horse clears the fences at a New York race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Mounts and jumps suggest horse racing, fitting the surface, but one is a direction signal and the other a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Saratoga Springs is a city in upstate New York famous for its historic thoroughbred racecourse.

clue.text: Descriptive phrase used by English PM about ambassador

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed around the other

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
William Pitt the Younger, and his father, were British Prime Ministers
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A characterising phrase that a British Prime Minister applied to a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: The ambassador's title goes inside the Prime Minister's name, between the two Ts.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a word or phrase characterising a person, such as the Great in Alfred the Great.

clue.text: After end of round, is hospital attendant confused?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only that letter is kept
after places what follows behind the first part, giving the order

blocks.note: the final letter of round
taken as written
an orderly is a hospital attendant

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a hospital porter is muddled after finishing his ward round.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorderly means untidy and in disarray, a looser synonym of confused or muddled.

clue.text: A worker, after advance, is to give assistance

indicators.note: the word placed after another comes second, so this tells the order of the two parts

blocks.note: to advance money is to lend it
taken as written
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A labourer, having received a loan, is expected to help out.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend a hand is an idiom meaning to help someone with a task.

clue.text: Tracks secretive birds

blocks.note: first meaning: the steel bars a train runs on
second meaning: shy marsh birds that hide in reeds

explanation.surface: Someone following the trail of shy birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracks reads as a verb, following the birds, but it is a plural noun for one meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway lines are made of steel bars, and the same word names a family of skulking wetland birds such as the water rail.

clue.text: One having a relationship with a much younger partner lends character somehow

definitions.text: One having a relationship with a much younger partner

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive by some unspecified route, so they are to be rearranged

blocks.note: the two words supply the letters

explanation.surface: A May-December romance supposedly gives a person a certain distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: Cradle-snatcher is an informal, mocking label for someone who dates a person far younger than themselves.

clue.text: Stealthily searching her plot now, surprisingly

indicators.note: a surprise is something unexpected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: the three words supply the letters

explanation.surface: A gardener quietly looking over her allotment after an unexpected change.
explanation.definitionFit: On the prowl is an idiom for moving about stealthily in search of prey or a target.

clue.text: Girl Irish boy recalled

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the name is read in the backward direction

blocks.note: Aidan is a common Irish boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl remembering an Irish lad from her past.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadia is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Demolishes residence and gets a standing ovation?

blocks.note: first meaning, taken literally: knocks a home to the ground
second meaning: the idiom for a show that thrills the whole theatre

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the literal wrecking sense and the theatre idiom are the same phrase; here house also means a theatre audience.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a performance so successful that the audience erupts in applause, while the literal words mean flattening a building.

clue.text: Lose one's temper and hit a female before work

indicators.note: before means coming ahead of, so it sets the order of the parts

blocks.note: a blow is a hit
taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female
to work something is to use it

explanation.surface: A violent outburst described as an instruction to lash out at a woman before going to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Blow a fuse is an idiom for suddenly becoming very angry, like an overloaded electrical circuit.

clue.text: See 14
Odd coin in vase depicting imaginary creature

indicators.note: something odd is irregular or strange, so the letters are rearranged
in says one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
an urn is a vase

explanation.surface: A strange coin found inside a vase decorated with a mythical beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A unicorn is a mythical horse with a single horn, so an example of a creature that does not exist.

clue.text: Individual going round eastern capital

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a soul is a person, as in not a soul about
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A lone traveller touring a capital city in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Seoul is the capital city of South Korea.

clue.text: A number of books in one vehicle

definitions.text: A number of books in one

blocks.clueFragment: A number of books in one
blocks.note: first meaning: a single volume collecting several works
second meaning: the old name for a bus

explanation.surface: Several books piled into a single car.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus edition gathers several books in one volume, and the word is also the full form of bus.

clue.text: Dancer, demure, attending a masquerade with the Queen in Austria's capital

indicators.note: a capital is the head letter of a word, so only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: prim means demure and proper
taken as written
a masquerade is a masked ball
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina
taken as written
the first letter of Austria

explanation.surface: A modest dancer goes to a masked ball in Vienna with the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Austria's capital tempts you towards Vienna, but here capital just means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima ballerina is the leading female dancer of a ballet company, so she is a particular kind of dancer.

clue.text: Departed on river afterwards

blocks.note: late means dead, departed
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone set off on a river trip and did something afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Later and afterwards are synonyms for at a subsequent time.

clue.text: One was first to go round shop

indicators.note: going round turns something about, so the combined letters are read backwards

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: A shop that was the first to open in the area.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling cooked meats and cheeses.

clue.text: Like Humpty-Dumpty, round and vacant?

blocks.note: the letter O is round in shape
void means empty or vacant

explanation.surface: A description of the nursery-rhyme egg as round and empty-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: Humpty-Dumpty is drawn as an egg, and ovoid means egg-shaped.

clue.text: Not up to guarding 10? That's indefensible

indicators.note: to guard something is to surround and protect it, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: not up to a task means unable to do it
the number written as a word

explanation.surface: Someone incapable of defending a position: their case cannot be defended.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 looks like a cross-reference to the clue 10 across, but it is just the number.
explanation.definitionFit: An untenable position cannot be held or defended, a synonym of indefensible.

clue.text: Aryan rule? Unfortunately, for about 354 days

indicators.note: an unfortunate outcome is one that went wrong, so the letters are set out in a changed order

blocks.note: the two words supply the letters

explanation.surface: A remark on an unhappy period of racial supremacy lasting under a year.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve cycles of the moon's phases add up to roughly 354 days, a period shorter than the solar calendar year.

clue.text: Group inside makes us high-class Japanese dish

indicators.note: a group of letters sitting inside the words that follow is the thing to find

blocks.note: the run of letters spans the end of makes, all of us and the start of high

explanation.surface: Eating in company supposedly lends refinement to a Japanese meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is vinegared rice with raw fish, a famous dish from Japan.
